title: I Helped 60 Etsy Sellers BLOW UP Their Shops
key_points: A shop with 5,000 orders from only 35 listings indicates high product quality and repeat sales or multi-item purchases
Facebook Marketplace style photos need to be elevated to reflect product quality, along with updating labeling
Product-focused SEO misses traffic opportunities; customer-focused SEO targets new profitable customers
A digital shop with 11,900 sales at super low price points likely generated under $1,000 per year over 9 years due to listing fees and Etsy's percentage
SVG sellers should target B2B market instead of individual users for more consistent revenue
Typography is the biggest issue for graphic shops - must use updated modern font pairings and font duos of the current year
White background SVG thumbnails alone are insufficient - more needs to be done to get customer clicks
Product should take up at least 80% of the thumbnail; backgrounds should not have higher contrast than the product
Avoid Amazon-style white background listings on Etsy
No holiday listings until you have at least 100 orders
Long tail keywords (3 or more words making a searchable phrase) are preferred over short tail keyword stuffing
18 types of photos give higher conversion rates
Whitewash shiplap backgrounds and eucalyptus in mockups or photos should be avoided entirely
Loss leaders are inexpensive items under $20 with the goal of selling 20 times per day (140 orders per week) - not just cheap items sitting in shop
Only duplicate listings that have shown proof of concept; duplicating unproven listings creates dead listings fast
Avoid turquoise, teal, coral, and mustard color combinations, or adding purple to these - avoid this year
Good starting goal for low price point digital products is 100 orders per month
The 'in my era' vibe did well about 2.5 years ago; heart-in-middle designs did well 4-5 years ago - both are now outdated
Digital product sellers have scaled to over $117,000 per month, especially with utilitarian products that help save time, save money, or make money
Build product mix to serve customer in different areas of their life for 4-7 years to increase lifetime value
summary:
The video reviews approximately 20 Etsy shops that submitted for review 6 months prior, examining their current state and identifying common problems preventing sales growth. The presenter evaluates shops across handmade, digital products, print-on-demand, and laser businesses.

A recurring theme across nearly all shops is product-focused SEO versus customer-focused SEO. The presenter repeatedly emphasizes that sellers are missing profitable customers because their SEO describes what the product is rather than who would buy it and why. Long tail keywords of three or more words forming searchable phrases are recommended over short tail keyword stuffing. Examples given include transforming location-specific product descriptions into customer-intent searches like 'UK travel postcard' or 'England wall art for powder bathroom.'

Thumbnail and photography problems are identified in almost every shop reviewed. Specific issues include: products not taking up at least 80% of the thumbnail, backgrounds with higher contrast than products, busy distracting backgrounds, text too small to read on mobile, outdated mockups with shiplap and eucalyptus, pattern-on-pattern same-color combinations, artificial lighting, tile backgrounds, and kitchen counter settings. The presenter states there are 18 types of photos that give higher conversion rates.

Typography and font issues appear throughout the reviews. The presenter emphasizes that modern font pairings and font duos need to be current year, that many shops are using outdated fonts, and that text overlays are frequently overused - including full sentences with punctuation that should be removed. For digital product shops especially, the design quality visible in banners and thumbnails directly affects customer trust.

Pricing strategy and loss leaders are addressed with specific metrics. A loss leader is defined not as any cheap item but as an inexpensive item under $20 with the goal of selling 20 times per day or 140 orders per week. Inexpensive products that aren't selling create dead weight. The presenter notes that digital shops with very low price points and thousands of sales often translate to under $1,000 per year in revenue. One example of success given is digital product sellers scaling to over $117,000 per month, particularly with utilitarian products.

Additional specific recommendations include: no holiday listings until reaching 100 orders, avoiding duplicating listings without proof of concept, avoiding specific color combinations (turquoise/teal/coral/mustard/purple) this year, targeting B2B customers for SVG and pattern sellers, and building product mixes to serve customers across different areas of their life for 4-7 years. The presenter mentions having a 68-page guide with 40 trends for sellers in their coaching program.
